bill.title: National Plan for Epilepsy Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

industries.rationale: The bill's focus on epilepsy treatment, diagnosis, and cure research directly affects pharmaceutical and medical device companies developing epilepsy therapies.
The national plan's coordination of epilepsy care and services would affect hospitals and health systems that diagnose and treat epilepsy patients.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to create and carry out a national plan to address epilepsy, including prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and research coordination across federal agencies. HHS must establish an advisory council that reports to Congress every two years and must itself submit annual progress reports with recommended actions. These requirements would remain in effect until the end of 2035.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone whose personal data is held by a company.

bill.title: Patients Deserve Price Tags Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 522.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new price-disclosure obligations on hospitals and surgical centers, changing their administrative and compliance requirements.
Medical device costs must be included in the price estimates, affecting how device manufacturers' products are priced and disclosed to patients.
Price transparency requirements may affect how insurers negotiate rates and how patients understand their coverage and out-of-pocket costs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, and other healthcare facilities to provide patients with upfront price estimates for scheduled procedures and services. The estimates would need to include costs for the facility, physicians, anesthesia, medical devices, and other associated charges. Facilities that fail to provide these price disclosures could face civil penalties.

Insulin cost caps or coverage mandates would alter health insurers' benefit design and reimbursement structures.
Changes to insulin pricing and access may affect prescribing practices and patient cost-sharing at the point of care.

bill.plainSummary: The bill's title suggests it addresses insulin pricing or access, likely building on previous INSULIN Act proposals that capped out-of-pocket costs for insulin users. The subject terms indicate it may involve competition rules, administrative enforcement, and oversight of drug pricing.

bill.title: A bill to amend the Food Security Act of 1985 to add the emergency watershed program as a covered program for purposes of carrying out the regional conservation partnership program, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

industries.rationale: The bill modifies conservation partnership programs that directly affect farming and ranching operations participating in watershed and land conservation efforts.
Emergency watershed programs typically involve infrastructure work such as erosion control, flood prevention structures, and land stabilization projects.
Watershed programs address water quality and management issues that overlap with water utility and watershed management operations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would amend the Food Security Act of 1985 to include the Emergency Watershed Program as an eligible program under the Regional Conservation Partnership Program. The change would allow watershed emergency projects to be coordinated with other conservation efforts through the partnership framework. The bill appears narrowly focused on this administrative adjustment to conservation program eligibility.

districtAwards.description:
FOR THE PROJECT, “LOW-EMISSIONS, COLD-AGGLOMERATED IRON ORE BRIQUETTE FOR CLEANER STEEL,” VALE USA 
LLC (“VALE”) WILL CONSTRUCT A FIRST-OF-A-KIND FACILITY IN THE UNITED STATES (U.S.) TO LAUNCH A 
VIABLE LOW-EMISSIONS ALTERNATIVE IN THE IRON ORE PROCESS THAT CAN BE REPLICABLE AT BOTH DIRECT 
REDUCED IRON (DRI) AND BLAST FURNACE (BF) FACILITIES, MEETING THE DEMAND FOR LOW-EMISSIONS ORE-BASED 
METALLICS. VALE’S COLD-AGGLOMERATION IRON ORE BRIQUETTE (BQT) WILL DELIVER SIGNIFICANT REDUCTIONS IN 
FACILITY GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS COMPARED TO PROCESSES USED TO MAKE TRADITIONAL DRI PELLETS. VALE’S 
FACILITY WILL ALSO ENABLE A CIRCULAR APPROACH WHEREBY IRON ORE FINES AND METALLIC FINES GENERATED 
ON-SITE CAN BE REINCORPORATED INTO THE IRON ORE BRIQUETTE MANUFACTURING PROCESS, DRIVING ADDITIONAL 
OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCIES AND REDUCED EMISSIONS THROUGH AVOIDANCE OF THE SALE AND TRANSPORT OF FINES 
OFFSITE. VALE PLANS TO LICENSE THE COLD-AGGLOMERATION PROCESS FOR USE WITHIN THE U.S. METALLICS AND 
STEEL INDUSTRY TO PROPEL REPLICATION. THE PROJECT PLANS TO PROVIDE TANGIBLE BENEFITS TO THE 
COMMUNITY INCLUDING, FOR EXAMPLE, GENERATING AN ESTIMATED 150 NEW, SKILLED, WELL-PAYING JOBS AND 
ENGAGING AND CONTRACTING UNION WORKFORCE WHEREVER FEASIBLE. VALE’S COMMUNITY BENEFITS COMMITMENTS 
WILL BE SHAPED TO DRIVE SUSTAINABLE LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND WILL INCLUDE FIRM COMMITMENTS TO 
INVEST IN WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AT THE FACILITY. THE PROJECT WILL PAY PREVAILING WAGES, ENSURE 
EQUITABLE ACCESS TO TRADITIONALLY UNDERSERVED GROUPS, PROVIDE INTERNSHIP OR APPRENTICESHIP 
OPPORTUNITIES FOR POTENTIAL LOCAL HIRES, AND PURSUE NEGOTIATED WORKFORCE AGREEMENTS, COMMUNITY 
AGREEMENTS, AND PARTNERSHIPS. THE PROJECT WILL INVEST IN SUPPORT TO ENSURE EQUITABLE ACCESS TO JOB 
OPPORTUNITIES FOR LOCAL WORKERS.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
